solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique, linked answer split by the grid); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Means to paint walls of study, receiving request

indicators.note: the word for study is split open to form walls on either side of what goes in
receiving means the study word takes the request word inside it

parts.note: to scan a page is to study it closely
to pray is to request, as in 'pray tell'

explanation.surface: Someone decorating the walls of a study is asked for something mid-job.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Walls of' and 'receiving' are both containment signals; the painting of walls in the surface is a red herring for decorating.
explanation.definitionFit: An aerosol of paint is a tool, or means, for painting graffiti and touch-ups.

clue.text: Funny part of drink that's mixed with some coke

parts.note: punch is a drink mixed from several ingredients
a line is a single dose of cocaine laid out to be snorted

explanation.surface: A party drink is being stirred together with a little cocaine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mixed' looks like an anagram signal but belongs to the description of punch; 'coke' here is cocaine, not the soft drink.
explanation.definitionFit: The closing line that delivers a joke's laugh is the funny part of it.

clue.text: Duck keen to seize egg

indicators.note: to seize means the keen word grabs and holds the egg shape within it

parts.note: avid means keen or eager
an egg is O-shaped, so it gives the letter O

explanation.surface: An eager duck is about to grab an egg.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Duck' is the verb, to dodge, not the bird the surface suggests.
explanation.definitionFit: To duck a question or a blow is to sidestep or evade it.

clue.text: Where punters are turning up computer game

indicators.note: in a down clue, turning up means the computer word is read bottom to top, backwards

parts.note: a Mac is an Apple computer
bridge is a card game

explanation.surface: Gamblers arrive to play a video game on a computer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Punters' suggests gamblers; here they are people in punts, flat boats pushed with a pole along the River Cam, a famous Cambridge pastime.
explanation.definitionFit: Punting on the river is a signature leisure activity in this English university city.

clue.text: Back home, given common salt

indicators.note: back means the word for home is read in reverse

parts.note: to be in is to be at home
trite means common or hackneyed

explanation.surface: Returning home, someone is handed ordinary table salt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Common salt' looks like one phrase for sodium chloride; split it, with 'common' giving TRITE and 'salt' alone the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A nitrite is a chemical salt of nitrous acid, used for example in curing meat.

clue.text: Pudding? I'm not sure it's a fool

parts.note: duff is a boiled pudding, as in plum duff
er is the sound of hesitation or uncertainty

explanation.surface: Someone hesitates over a dessert: is it a pudding, or is it a fool?
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fool' is also a fruit-and-cream dessert, which makes the pudding talk seem connected; here it means an incompetent person.
explanation.definitionFit: An inept, bumbling person is a synonym for an idiot or a fool.

clue.text: Rectify IT errors in half of code with virus

indicators.note: half of means only the back two letters of the four-letter word code are used

parts.note: a bug is a virus, as in a stomach bug

explanation.surface: Fixing computer faults found in part of the code, along with a virus.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Half of' takes the second half of CODE, DE; 'virus' means an illness, a bug, rather than malware.
explanation.definitionFit: To debug software is to find and remove faults from a program.

clue.text: Favouring new tea set one's delivered by trailer

parts.note: to be for something is to favour it

indicators.note: new signals that the letters of tea set are made into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Someone who likes the new tea set has it delivered by a lorry trailer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'New' makes ETASTE from TEA SET; 'trailer' looks like a vehicle but means a preview.
explanation.definitionFit: A film trailer is a preview, giving a sample in advance of the full thing.

clue.text: Browser requiring electronic money

parts.note: E is the standard abbreviation for electronic, as in e-mail
quid is British slang for a pound, so money

explanation.surface: A web browser that needs online money to work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Browser' suggests web software; here it is an animal that browses on leaves.
explanation.definitionFit: Horses, donkeys and zebras belong to the horse family, plant-eaters that graze and browse.

clue.text: Playing well, do some singing

definitions.meaning: a sportsperson on good form is playing well
to sing is slang for telling the police

explanation.surface: A performer is on good form and does some singing.
explanation.definitionFit: Read as two words it means on good form; as one it means to grass to the police.

clue.text: Military leader who ruled Beirut is toppled

indicators.note: toppled means knocked over, so the letters of Beirut is fall into a new order

explanation.surface: A general who once governed the Lebanese capital has been overthrown.
explanation.definitionFit: The second Roman emperor was a successful general before he ruled the empire.

clue.text: Ex-PM's dear American friends in TV programme

parts.note: a sweetheart addressed as dear is the beloved one, the loved one
bud is American slang for a friend
Theresa May is a former British Prime Minister, so the possessive becomes 'of May'

explanation.surface: A former Prime Minister's beloved friends from the United States turn up in a television show.
explanation.walkthrough: Rephrase the possessive 'X's Y' as 'the Y of X': May's dear buds become the dear buds of May, with the possessive moved to the end.
explanation.definitionFit: This ITV comedy-drama of the early 1990s followed the Larkin family in 1950s rural Kent.

clue.text: State of commotion as yet unrealised

definitions.meaning: still waiting to be done, like items on a task list

explanation.surface: A disturbance whose consequences have not yet been seen.
explanation.definitionFit: Hyphenated it is a fuss; as two words it describes jobs still pending.

clue.text: Be involved with raid? This is blown up at night

definitions.text: This is blown up at night

indicators.note: involved means twisted up together, so the letters of be and raid are mixed into a new order

explanation.surface: A question about joining a raid, followed by a hint of something exploding after dark.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Blown up' suggests a bombing raid; here it is inflated with air.
explanation.definitionFit: An inflatable mattress is pumped full of air for sleeping on overnight.

clue.text: See 11
Request for attention in dance

definitions.meaning: a polite phrase used to get someone's attention
a ballroom dance in which a partner may be cut in on by another

explanation.surface: Someone politely asks for attention on the dance floor.
explanation.definitionFit: The polite phrase also names a dance where others may interrupt to change partners.

clue.text: Parrot or cuckoo to cackle around island

indicators.note: around means the scrambled letters surround the island letter
cuckoo means crazy, so the letters of to cackle are scrambled

explanation.surface: A parrot, or perhaps a cuckoo, is cackling somewhere on an island.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cuckoo' looks like a second bird beside 'Parrot', but it means mad and is the anagram signal; 'around' puts the mixed letters, COCKATEL, around I.
explanation.definitionFit: This small crested Australian bird is a member of the cockatoo family of parrots.

clue.text: Footballer gathers in a shot Celtic's Number 1 is liable to save?

parts.note: Lionel Messi is the Argentine footballer

indicators.note: shot means wrecked or ruined, so the letters of in a are jumbled
number 1 means the first letter of Celtic is taken

explanation.surface: A footballer's shot that Celtic's goalkeeper might be expected to save.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shot' and 'save' sound like football; 'shot' rearranges IN A into ANI, and 'Number 1' is not the goalkeeper but the first letter, C.
explanation.definitionFit: A messiah is a saviour, so someone with a saviour complex is inclined to rescue others.

clue.text: Feeling nothing, getting smacked bum

parts.note: a numb limb is dead, without sensation
beat means smacked or struck

explanation.surface: Someone feels nothing after having their bottom smacked.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bum' looks like the part being smacked; it is the US sense of a layabout.
explanation.definitionFit: A lazy, idle person who avoids work is a layabout or loafer.

clue.text: European country defending new and old guard

indicators.note: defending means the country wraps around and protects the letter for new

parts.note: Turkey is a country partly in Europe

explanation.surface: A European nation protecting both its new recruits and its veterans.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Old guard' looks like the conservative establishment; it means a jailer of old.
explanation.definitionFit: An archaic word for a jailer, the warder who held the keys to the cells.

clue.text: Like a fondue with lots of corn

definitions.meaning: a fondue is melted cheese, so full of cheese

explanation.surface: A dish resembling a fondue, served with plenty of sweetcorn.
explanation.definitionFit: Full of cheese suits a fondue; it also means corny, tacky and sentimental.

clue.text: Return of old French way to make French bread

indicators.note: return means the letters for old and French way are read backwards

parts.note: rue is French for street, a way

explanation.surface: Bringing back the traditional French method of baking bread.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bread' is slang for money, so French bread is French currency, not a baguette.
explanation.definitionFit: Bread is slang for money, and this is the currency used in France.

clue.text: Escort person with a habit astride horse

indicators.note: astride means the person's letters sit either side of the horse letter, like legs over a saddle

parts.note: a user is someone with a drug habit
horse is slang for heroin, abbreviated H

explanation.surface: A nun, wearing her habit, rides a horse as an escort.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Person with a habit' suggests a nun or monk; it is a drug user, and 'horse' is heroin.
explanation.definitionFit: To show someone to their seat, as at a theatre or wedding, is to escort them.

clue.text: He wants no breaks in air lock? How odd!

indicators.note: odd means strange, signalling that the letters of air lock how are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone who wants no interruptions in a spaceship's air lock, which is odd.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Breaks' suggests cracks in an air lock; it means rest breaks from work.
explanation.definitionFit: A person compulsively devoted to their job refuses time off or rest.

clue.text: Comment from setter, say, about Latin writer

indicators.note: about means the dog's comment goes around the Latin letter

parts.note: a setter is a breed of dog, and a dog's comment is a bark

explanation.surface: The crossword compiler remarks on a classical author.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Setter' looks like the crossword compiler; here it is the dog breed.
explanation.definitionFit: Virginia, the modernist novelist of Mrs Dalloway, is a famous English author.

clue.text: Ancient king and leader in legend shows guts

parts.note: Offa was an eighth-century king of Mercia, famous for Offa's Dyke

indicators.note: leader in means the first letter of legend is taken

explanation.surface: An old king and a legendary leader display great courage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Guts' looks like bravery; it means entrails. Offa was an Anglo-Saxon king in central England.
explanation.definitionFit: Animal entrails and organs used as food are called by this name.

clue.text: Synthetic music is a feature on March 17

parts.note: sham means fake or synthetic
rock is a genre of music

explanation.surface: Electronic music forms part of a celebration in mid-March.
explanation.walkthrough: March 17 is St Patrick's Day, when the three-leaved plant emblem of Ireland is worn.
explanation.definitionFit: The Irish clover emblem is worn and displayed everywhere on St Patrick's Day.

clue.text: Cool carbonated drink, but not a little one

parts.note: in means fashionable or cool

indicators.note: but not means the letter a is dropped from the drink's name

parts.note: Fanta is a fizzy orange soft drink

explanation.surface: A chilled fizzy drink is fine, but not one for a small child.
explanation.definitionFit: A baby or very young child is a little one.

clue.text: Shriek loudly, welcoming United's star player

indicators.note: welcoming means the shriek takes the United letter inside it

parts.note: to cry is to shriek
U is the standard abbreviation for United, as in football club names
ff, fortissimo, is the musical mark for very loudly

explanation.surface: A fan screams loudly as a United star arrives.
explanation.walkthrough: Johan Cruyff was the great Dutch footballer of Ajax and Barcelona, never of any United.
explanation.definitionFit: The Dutch forward was one of the outstanding footballers of the 1970s.

clue.text: University rugby player's safety device

parts.note: Yale is an American Ivy League university
a lock is a second-row forward in rugby

explanation.surface: A college rugby player owns a piece of protective equipment.
explanation.walkthrough: In rugby, a lock is a second-row forward position.
explanation.definitionFit: This brand of cylinder door fastener keeps a home secure.
